Ohio State Buckeyes.career_experience: Not addressed in guide as a career summary; the guide treats him as the established starter.
Ohio State Buckeyes.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide notes Arthur Smith will let Sayin use his legs.
Ohio State Buckeyes.competition: None described — Sayin is the settled starter.
Ohio State Buckeyes.author_confidence: High. Sayin and Jeremiah Smith are called arguably the best quarterback-receiver combination in the country.
Ohio State Buckeyes.positive_case: Arguably the best quarterback-receiver combination in the country, on one of the sport's most talented rosters, with the guide expecting the training wheels to come off.
Ohio State Buckeyes.concerns: Not addressed in guide as a quarterback concern; the guide's reservations are 51 newcomers and the schedule.
Ohio State Buckeyes.scheme_fit: Expected to change in his favour. Ohio State ran the slowest-paced offense in college football, and the guide expects Arthur Smith to loosen it — suggesting Smith could do for the offense what Patricia did for the defense — while wanting to run more aggressively and letting Sayin use his legs.
Ohio State Buckeyes.supporting_cast: Elite. Jeremiah Smith is described as the most talented receiver in college football since arriving as a true freshman, to the point that No. 4 overall pick Carnell Tate was the second option; Brandon Inniss returns, Chris Henry Jr is the latest five-star freshman, and transfer Devin McCuin had 726 yards and eight touchdowns at UTSA. Four offensive line starters return and Bo Jackson ran for almost 1,100 yards as a freshman behind them.
Ohio State Buckeyes.portal_context: 18 portal additions, 50 new players and another top-five recruiting class; Devin McCuin arrives at receiver from UTSA.
Ohio State Buckeyes.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 9.5 wins. The guide notes a single-digit total would ordinarily be an obvious Over given Ohio State has not won fewer than ten in a full season since 2011, setting against that 51 newcomers and a loaded schedule.
Ohio State Buckeyes.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The quarterback is treated as a settled strength rather than a risk; the guide's stated risks are roster turnover and schedule.

Oregon Ducks.status: Returning starter — turned down the NFL Draft.
Oregon Ducks.career_experience: Junior; 2025 was his first year starting at Oregon.
Oregon Ducks.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Oregon Ducks.passing: 3,565 yards and 30 touchdowns in his first year starting.
Oregon Ducks.turnovers: Four turnovers across the two meetings with Indiana, including a pick-six on the opening snap of the Peach Bowl.
Oregon Ducks.competition: None described — Moore is the settled starter.
Oregon Ducks.author_confidence: High on production, explicitly open on the biggest stage. The guide calls him justifiably a Heisman favorite and expects monster numbers again, while keeping the big-stage question open.
Oregon Ducks.positive_case: Heisman-favorite production with abundant support, on a roster the guide says may be the most talented in college football.
Oregon Ducks.concerns: Big-game performance. The guide cites the two meetings with Indiana in which Moore was sacked nine times with four turnovers, including a pick-six on the opening snap of the Peach Bowl.
Oregon Ducks.supporting_cast: Deep. Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr combined for 1,323 rushing yards as freshman backups, sophomore receivers Dakorien Moore and Jeremiah McClellan should start, and Evan Stewart returns from a knee injury. The line is the stated risk: Rimington Trophy finalist Iapani Laloulu anchors at center for a third season with Dave Iuli back at right guard, but three starters need replacing — and the guide poses a genuine puzzle about why the only line to be a Joe Moore Award finalist three years running struggles in big games, citing 11 three-and-outs, 11 sacks allowed and 21 tackles for loss across two playoff exits.
Oregon Ducks.portal_context: Not addressed in guide for the quarterback position.
Oregon Ducks.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 10.5 wins, with the guide immediately conceding there is never much margin for error above 10.5, especially with trips to USC and Ohio State. What must go right: the offensive line gelling, and young skill players stepping up from productive backup roles.
Oregon Ducks.outlook_dependency: High. Oregon returns 66% of net production headlined by Moore turning down the draft, and the guide's title case runs through him performing when it matters most.

Penn State Nittany Lions.status: Transfer — from Iowa State, arriving with head coach Matt Campbell.
Penn State Nittany Lions.career_experience: Made 39 consecutive starts at Iowa State.
Penn State Nittany Lions.competition: None described — Becht is presented as the starter, with the guide's concern being availability rather than competition.
Penn State Nittany Lions.backup: Thin and injured. Fellow Iowa State transfer Alex Manske also missed spring with injury, and Connor Barry, a Division III transfer from Christopher Newport, is the only other quarterback on the roster to have taken a college snap.
Penn State Nittany Lions.author_confidence: Positive but conditioned entirely on health — the guide's question is literally whether Becht can stay healthy.
Penn State Nittany Lions.positive_case: 39 consecutive starts, arriving with his head coach, his coordinator and his top four pass catchers from Iowa State.
Penn State Nittany Lions.concerns: Durability. He made those starts despite a torn labrum, a sprained AC joint and two concussions last season, then had offseason surgery limiting him to 7-on-7 work — behind a depth chart with almost no experience.
Penn State Nittany Lions.scheme_fit: Maximal continuity — Campbell brought 11 assistants including coordinator Taylor Mouser plus 24 players from Ames.
Penn State Nittany Lions.supporting_cast: Familiar. Running back Carson Hansen (1,771 yards, 19 touchdowns over two years) plus Ben Brahmer, Gabe Burkle, Chase Sowell and Brett Eskildsen — his top four pass catchers at Iowa State — with Ohio State transfer James Peoples and Quentin Martin Jr adding backfield depth.
Penn State Nittany Lions.portal_context: Campbell brought 24 from Iowa State within 40 total transfers, as Penn State replaces 70 players including eight drafted last spring. Thirty-six of the 40 are from Power Four schools; the guide draws an explicit comparison with Cignetti's 29 transfers to Indiana in 2024 and closes with the caution that the Big Ten is still a step above the Big 12.
Penn State Nittany Lions.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 9.5 wins, built through a comparison — pundits spent last season asking who the next Indiana would be, and the guide suggests Penn State this year. Penn State avoids Ohio State, Oregon and Indiana entirely, travels to Michigan and Washington, and should be favored in every home game.
Penn State Nittany Lions.outlook_dependency: High, and specifically on availability. The guide's lead quarterback question is health, and the backup situation is described as thin.

Purdue Boilermakers.status: Returning starter — no portal quarterback was added, so the job is his again.
Purdue Boilermakers.career_experience: Incumbent starter who played through an ankle injury in 2025.
Purdue Boilermakers.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Purdue Boilermakers.passing: 2,153 yards with nine touchdowns to ten interceptions.
Purdue Boilermakers.turnovers: Ten interceptions against nine touchdown passes.
Purdue Boilermakers.competition: None — the guide states explicitly that no portal quarterback was added, making this Browne's job again.
Purdue Boilermakers.author_confidence: Mixed but fair. The guide holds Browne to improvement while noting fairly that he had little help, and lists a settled quarterback among the reasons four wins is doable.
Purdue Boilermakers.positive_case: A settled quarterback situation, with far more skill-position help arriving and better line personnel.
Purdue Boilermakers.concerns: A negative touchdown-to-interception ratio while playing hurt, in an offense that struggled in short yardage (85th on third downs) and the red zone (119th).
Purdue Boilermakers.supporting_cast: Substantially rebuilt. Second-leading rusher Antonio Harris (69 carries, 305 yards, two touchdowns) returns, but most production should come from portal additions: running backs Fame Ijeboi (Minnesota), Jerrick Gibson (Texas) and Travis Terrell (Jackson State), plus three portal receivers all expected to start — Bisi Owens (Penn), Assad Wassem (Florida Atlantic) and Xavier Townsend (Iowa State) — with De'Nylon Morrissette back from an ankle injury. Left tackle Joey Tanona returns with as many as four new portal starters possible.
Purdue Boilermakers.portal_context: Heavy at the skill positions and on the offensive line, but deliberately not at quarterback. Odom fired offensive line coach Vance Vice, who had come with him from UNLV, and hired Zach Crabtree, previously with coordinator Josh Henson at USC; the guide rates the change an upgrade.
Purdue Boilermakers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 3.5 wins. The guide is candid that Purdue is far from the competitiveness of the Jeff Brohm years while rating Odom and staff an upgrade on Ryan Walters' tenure, and concludes that a settled quarterback, better line personnel and some conference games with a smaller talent gap make four wins doable — but that is likely the ceiling.
Purdue Boilermakers.outlook_dependency: Moderate. A settled quarterback is one of three stated reasons four wins is achievable, and the guide caps the ceiling regardless.

Rutgers Scarlet Knights.status: Transfer — from Boston College; described as likely to win the job rather than confirmed.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.previous_school: Boston College; previously taken to Alabama by Nick Saban as a four-star recruit.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.career_experience: Nine starts at Boston College; once a four-star recruit at Alabama.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.passing: 66.9% completions for 2,025 yards with 12 touchdowns to five interceptions across nine starts.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.competition: Live. Sophomore AJ Surace saw limited action behind Athan Kaliakmanis and now faces Lonergan; the guide expects Lonergan to win.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.backup: Sophomore AJ Surace, who saw limited action behind Kaliakmanis.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.author_confidence: Moderate. The guide expects Lonergan to win the job and expects points regardless, without making a strong claim about him.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.positive_case: Efficient nine-start production at Boston College, with weapons available around him.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.concerns: Replacing a two-year starter in Athan Kaliakmanis, behind a line with three spots open going into camp.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.scheme_fit: Not addressed in guide directly; the guide argues Schiano and coordinator Kirk Ciarrocca must play more ball control given the defensive problems.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.supporting_cast: Better than Rutgers usually retains. The guide makes a structural point in passing — Rutgers consistently has player retention problems because of NIL — yet kept running back Antwan Raymond (1,275 yards, 13 touchdowns) and 6-foot-6 receiver K.J. Duff (60 catches, 1,084 yards, seven touchdowns). The line returns senior starters Tyler Needham at left tackle and Kwabena Asamoah at right guard with three spots open; Hank Zilinskas (Colorado), Everett Small (Eastern Michigan) and Isaiah Cook (Delaware State) bring starting experience.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.portal_context: Lonergan and three offensive linemen arrived through the portal; the guide notes Rutgers is rebuilding its defense through the portal for a second straight season.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins. Even with the defensive problems the guide expects points, with Lonergan likely to win the job alongside Antwan Raymond and K.J. Duff — but it is clear the Over still requires winning a coin flip or two, naming Maryland and Northwestern away plus Michigan State.
Rutgers Scarlet Knights.outlook_dependency: High. The Over is argued from expected scoring, which the guide attaches to the quarterback plus the two retained skill players.

UCLA Bruins.status: Returning starter — the player who stayed through the coaching change.
UCLA Bruins.previous_school: Not applicable as a 2026 move — he had transferred from Tennessee before 2025.
UCLA Bruins.career_experience: 11 starts at UCLA in 2025 after transferring from Tennessee.
UCLA Bruins.passing: 1,929 passing yards in 11 starts, completing 64.4% with only seven interceptions.
UCLA Bruins.efficiency: 64.4% completions on low volume — the guide calls the season disappointing while noting the underlying detail is better than the raw yardage.
UCLA Bruins.turnovers: Seven interceptions — cited as a point in his favour.
UCLA Bruins.competition: None described — Iamaleava is the settled starter.
UCLA Bruins.author_confidence: Qualified but constructive. The guide records a disappointing first year in Westwood, then balances it with completion rate, interception count and rushing production.
UCLA Bruins.positive_case: Improved coaching — the new staff produced the nation's 16th-ranked offense at James Madison at 452.6 yards per game — plus 64.4% completions, low interceptions and genuine rushing production.
UCLA Bruins.concerns: Low passing volume, receivers who gave him little help, and a stylistic constraint: the guide says he is most effective throwing on the run rather than from the pocket, so receivers must create separation.
UCLA Bruins.scheme_fit: Favourable. Chesney brought eight James Madison assistants including coordinators Dean Kennedy and Colin Hitschler from a 16th-ranked offense.
UCLA Bruins.supporting_cast: Rebuilt. All-purpose back Wayne Knight arrives from James Madison (1,373 rushing yards, nine touchdowns, 397 receiving) alongside returning backs Jaivian Thomas and Anthony Woods and three offensive line starters in Riley Robell, Carter Sweezie — both All-Sun Belt — and JD Rayner. The receiving corps is essentially new: holdover Mikey Matthews plus Landon Ellis, Leland Smith, Brian Rowe, Aidan Mizell and Semaj Morgan, with Rowe rated the most talented, Ellis bringing 624 yards and familiarity with the offense, and Smith 43 catches for 688 yards and three touchdowns at San Jose State.
UCLA Bruins.portal_context: Chesney brought 10 of his 42 transfers from James Madison along with eight assistants.
UCLA Bruins.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins. The guide names the hope directly — that Westwood repeats what Cignetti did in Bloomington — rates the staff a massive upgrade on Deshaun Foster's group, and still calls the team a bit overpriced, concluding 6-6 is realistic but seven wins looks a reach.
UCLA Bruins.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's starting point is the quarterback who stayed, and its offensive case runs through whether he takes the next step with better coaching and receivers.

USC Trojans.career_experience: Not addressed in guide as a career summary; named among the 14 returning starters.
USC Trojans.competition: None described — Maiava is the settled starter.
USC Trojans.author_confidence: Implicitly positive but undeveloped. Maiava is named as part of what may be Riley's most talented group in five seasons; the guide's doubts are about the team's big-game record and a new coordinator, not the quarterback specifically.
USC Trojans.positive_case: Part of a group with 14 returning starters and the nation's No. 1 recruiting class, in an offense the guide expects to score plenty of points as always under Riley.
USC Trojans.concerns: Not addressed as a quarterback concern; the guide flags a new coordinator installing a new system, and that most of the recruiting class may be a year away from real impact.
USC Trojans.scheme_fit: Flagged as an unknown — the guide expresses concern about a new coordinator installing a new system.
USC Trojans.supporting_cast: Weakened at receiver, strong on the ground. Biletnikoff winner Makai Lemon and Ja'Kobi Lane take 1,900 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns with them; Tanook Hines (34 catches, 561 yards, two touchdowns) gets first chance as top target, with NC State transfer Terrell Anderson adding 628 yards at 16.1 per reception. The guide judges the group's talent slightly below USC's usual level and draws the tactical consequence that the Trojans may run more with King Miller and Waymond Jordan, who combined for over 1,500 yards and 15 touchdowns behind a line returning all five starters.
USC Trojans.portal_context: Terrell Anderson arrives at receiver from NC State.
USC Trojans.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins. USC avoids none of the elite Big Ten teams; after a soft September in which 4-0 is likely it is thrown into the deep end. The guide grounds its case in record — USC is 5-11 against ranked opposition in Riley's four seasons and 10-10 in true Big Ten road games — and concludes that until the Trojans prove it in big games this looks like a repeat of last season.
USC Trojans.outlook_dependency: Low to moderate. The guide's Under is argued from big-game and road record and from coordinator change, not from quarterback risk.

Washington Huskies.status: Returning starter — after entering the transfer portal and returning to Seattle.
Washington Huskies.career_experience: Established starter who led Washington to fourth nationally in scoring and fifth in total offense.
Washington Huskies.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Washington Huskies.passing: Across Washington's four defeats he managed just 645 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions. Team-level: fourth nationally in scoring at 34.1 points and fifth in total offense at 409.9 yards.
Washington Huskies.efficiency: Against the four best defenses Washington faced — Ohio State, Michigan, Wisconsin and Oregon — the Huskies averaged 9.3 points and 4.3 yards per play.
Washington Huskies.turnovers: Six interceptions across the four defeats.
Washington Huskies.competition: None described — Williams is the settled starter, with the guide's concern being commitment and big-game form rather than competition.
Washington Huskies.author_confidence: Positive on talent, pointed about the rest. The guide calls him among the conference's more dynamic quarterbacks if the portal episode is behind everyone, then insists he simply has to be better against better teams.
Washington Huskies.positive_case: He led Washington to fourth nationally in scoring at 34.1 points and fifth in total offense at 409.9 yards, and the guide treats his return as a necessary condition for the programme's next step.
Washington Huskies.concerns: Two: the near-departure, and big-game production. The guide records that days after signing a $4 million NIL deal to return, Williams entered the portal and was reportedly close to signing for more money with LSU; it did not reach court, and he returned. It suggests he received bad advice from his representatives. On the field, 645 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions across four defeats is the stated problem.
Washington Huskies.supporting_cast: Diminished at the skill positions, solid up front. Receiver Denzel Boston and running back Jonah Coleman are gone; receiver Dezmen Roebuck (42 catches, 560 yards, seven touchdowns) and tight end Decker DeGraaf return, with four-star receivers Jordan Clay, Mason James and Trez Davis part of Washington's highest-rated recruiting class in school history. At running back, Coleman's heir apparent Adam Mohammed transferred to Cal; seniors Jayden Limar (Oregon) and Trey Cooley (Troy) arrived but both missed spring with injuries, and Jordan Washington was also hurt, so redshirt freshman Quaid Carr and true freshman Brian Bonner took most reps. Four line starters return including the Hatchett brothers, center Landen and right guard Geirean, with five-star freshman Kodi Greene expected at left tackle.
Washington Huskies.portal_context: Williams himself entered and exited the portal. Jayden Limar and Trey Cooley arrived at running back; Adam Mohammed left for Cal.
Washington Huskies.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins. Washington opens with an all-home September, so 4-0 is expected before the trip to USC, which the guide suggests could build confidence toward finally beating a good team. The counterweight it supplies is the 9.3 points and 4.3 yards per play against the four best defenses faced.
Washington Huskies.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide states Williams' return is a necessary condition for the next step and puts the weight on him for the signature win Washington still lacks.

Wisconsin Badgers.status: Transfer — from Old Dominion; the fourth straight year Wisconsin's starting quarterback has come from the portal.
Wisconsin Badgers.career_experience: Sun Belt Player of the Year at Old Dominion.
Wisconsin Badgers.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide reports two seasons of production.
Wisconsin Badgers.passing: 4,251 passing yards and 32 touchdowns over two seasons.
Wisconsin Badgers.rushing: 1,654 rushing yards and 24 touchdowns over two seasons. The guide's sharpest illustration: Joseph individually had more runs of 10-plus yards last season, 37, than Wisconsin managed as a team, 33.
Wisconsin Badgers.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate.
Wisconsin Badgers.competition: None described — Joseph is presented as the starter.
Wisconsin Badgers.author_confidence: Positive on the player, pessimistic about what surrounds him. The guide sees him as a potential jolt and says he certainly makes the offense better, while judging the ceiling stays low with few proven playmakers.
Wisconsin Badgers.positive_case: Sun Belt Player of the Year production, and a running threat who individually out-produced the entire Wisconsin team in explosive runs.
Wisconsin Badgers.concerns: The context rather than the player: the worst scoring offense in the Power Four at 12.8 points per game, 133rd nationally, and 81 points across nine Big Ten games in 2025, with few proven playmakers around him.
Wisconsin Badgers.scheme_fit: Favourable in intent — coordinator Jeff Grimes is expected to go run-heavy, especially with a mobile quarterback, though the guide insists some receiver production is still required.
Wisconsin Badgers.supporting_cast: Thin. Very little receiving production returns — the leading receiver managed under 400 yards — with Chris Brooks Jr and Eugene Hilton back, joined by Oklahoma State transfer Shamar Rigby and Minnesota transfer Malachi Coleman. On the ground Wisconsin ranked 115th nationally at 116.7 yards per game; leading rusher Darrion Dupree (83 carries, 363 yards, two touchdowns) returns with Abu Sama III from Iowa State (1,933 yards, 13 touchdowns across three seasons) and USC transfer Bryan Jackson II. Three offensive line starters are back.
Wisconsin Badgers.portal_context: A complete roster makeover with 33 transfers; the guide judges the heavy portal reliance looks like a search for a quick fix.
Wisconsin Badgers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins. After the Notre Dame opener at Lambeau Field the schedule eases, with three of the next four at home and Wisconsin avoiding Ohio State, Oregon and Indiana — yet the guide judges seven wins a big ask for a team lacking talent at many positions.
Wisconsin Badgers.outlook_dependency: High. The guide states wins will stay scarce unless the offense improves, and Joseph is the named mechanism for that improvement — while capping the ceiling regardless.
